pull.title: torcontrol: Improve connection logging
pull.body:
Before eae193e750235e4023b3e6313284eede2cd7a022, Connect() only started the connection and returned true. If tor wasn't running the refusal was reported later and only logged under -debug=tor. Since eae193e750 (in v32), every failed reconnect attempt logs:

```
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z connect() to 127.0.0.1:9051 failed after wait: Connection refused (111)
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z [warning] tor: Error connecting to address 127.0.0.1:9051
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z [warning] tor: Initiating connection to Tor control port 127.0.0.1:9051 failed
```

On a default configured node without tor, this pollutes debug.log with 18 lines every hour.

This makes the following improvements:
- Log connection failures as warning if tor config is explicit set (`-torcontrol`, `-torpassword` or `-listenonion`), otherwise at debug level.
- Log at info level when an active onion service is lost.
- Log info at the first tor connection failure if no tor config is explicit set.

The first two commits are from @fjahr.

events.body:
I've noticed these annoying warnings as well on my own node without tor and looked into it. There is an exponential backoff with limit of `RECONNECT_TIMEOUT_MAX{600.0};   // 10 min cap` so after ~20 minutes or so the log messages drop to once every ten minutes. We keep attempting this connection so that if the user starts tor later in the node's lifetime, we just pick it up and work with it.

Personally I think it's annoying when you first start the node but then I dont mind seeing the attempts 6x/hour. Reminds me I need to start tor!

So I need help understanding the motivation for this change.

> So I need help understanding the motivation for this change.

My main motivation is that it can be confusing for users that are not running tor since it is a warning level message they might think it is a config error or open new issue (#36691) and also pollutes logs. If the user wants to see tor debug logs they can set -debug=tor like it was before v32

ACK ac6d31e7a9320773b98934478d0e2ea3c17dfb65

Built and tested on macos/arm64. Code changes are justified and makes the logs cleaner /  more like pre-32 behavior. Thanks @ViniciusCestarii for answering my questions!

Also wanted to throw out the option of using the new `LogWarnThenDebug()` if you think that makes sense. Happy to re review.

logs look less noisy (quite peaceful now) when i ran `bitcoind` in regtest

re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36759#pullrequestreview-5791717944

`LogWarnThenDebug` strikes a balance between various user needs, i think it is OK to take it up. the log message that shows failure to connect to tor control is logged exactly once. logs will look sth like this:

<details open><summary>logs</summary>

```text
...
2026-11-05T22:59:01Z torcontrol thread start
2026-11-05T22:59:01Z initload thread exit
2026-11-05T22:59:01Z [warning] Error connecting to address 127.0.0.1:9051
2026-11-05T22:59:01Z [warning] Initiating connection to Tor control port 127.0.0.1:9051 failed
2026-11-05T22:59:01Z Bound to 127.0.0.1:18445
2026-11-05T22:59:01Z Bound to [::]:18444
2026-11-05T22:59:01Z Bound to 0.0.0.0:18444
2026-11-05T22:59:01Z Loaded 0 addresses from "anchors.dat"
...
```

</details>

I agree that the current behavior isn't ideal but it seems that an bigger problem than noisy logs is that you wouldn't see any logs unless you had `-debug=tor` if you had `-torcontrol` set explicitly, i.e. you clearly want to use Tor but there is an issue and it doesn't work. That's why I think the current v32 behavior was an improvement to the previous behavior. Instead of reverting, I would suggest a more complete fix that works well for both scenarios: When the user configured Tor they should see logs and when they didn't they should not see them (only with `-debug=tor`).

I have drafted the change so people can decide if they like this more: https://github.com/fjahr/bitcoin/commits/2026-11-torlog/ But note that this also includes a bit of additional improvements like making the logging less noisy when it does happen and deals with losing the connection along the way.

> if you're OK with it, I can pull your commits into this PR

Sure, go ahead!

events.body: Force-pushed d5f6a9b6c96b30eaa9740eda5b9a98474a3aef59 adding @fjahr proposed changes + log the first failure once at info level. Updated PR title and description.

I think this has gotten perhaps too complicated. Even with Claude making me a chart I can't wrap my head around all the details:
- There's messages logging at Warn, Info, and Debug levels.
- There's torcontrol options being set manually and by default.
- There's the user's log level setting at default (info) or debug.
- There's first connection error and not-first error.
- There's a re-implementation of `LogWarnThenDebug()` but for Info level and then debug (I think?)
- Netbase and torcontrol both write logs, at different levels

I think we should discuss simpler logic that cleans up the log and still follows the guidelines about log level.

1. Always set "manual" to false" netbase only logs debug. Handle more interesting logging directly from torcontrol
2. Use LogWarnThenDebug instead of adding new state and effectively LogInfoThenDebug

I "generated" a commit along with @fjahr "lost connection" commit here: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...pinheadmz:bitcoin:torcontrol-log-simple


Tested by turning tor on and off during / before bitcoind. This feels right to me:

## default user
start with tor: `Got tor service ID...`
break tor: `Lost connection...` (only once)
restart tor: `Got tor service ID...`

start without tor: <nothing>
restart tor: `Got service ID...`
break tor: `Lost connection...` (only once)

## -listenonion / -torcontrol / -torpassword user
Same as default, plus a single `[warning] tor: Error connecting to address...` the first time any connection attempt fails (at startup if tor isn't running, or on the first reconnect attempt after tor breaks). Never repeated for the lifetime of the process.




## -debug user
logs every single retry attempt

comments.body: Why did you change this line? I think it actually shouldn't matter, its just residue of how all of our socket handling code has the perspective of bitcoin p2p even when that's not what we're doing with the socket.

996846efe6d0e7ee67d7fc7857321f46d26df1bc

I feel like the value should keep the name `m_tor_control_configured` that is declared by `init.cpp`. "Manual" connection doesn't make sense to me in the tor control context. For that matter, I also feel like the the value in netbase could probably also be renamed `log_as_info` (or `verbose_failure`) or something because it has no effect until `LogConnectFailure()` is called which could be called by P2P, torcontrol, Proxy, even bitcoin-cli...
